title: Xplore 101: your first search
author: Branch Executive Committee
summary: A short guide to finding papers in IEEE Xplore, IEEE's digital library of journals, conference papers and standards.
content:
IEEE Xplore (ieeexplore.ieee.org) is IEEE's digital library of journal articles, conference papers and standards. Anyone can search it and read titles and abstracts.

1. Start broad. Type two or three key terms into the search box, for example: solar irrigation Uganda.

2. Use quotation marks for exact phrases, such as "machine learning", so results contain the words together.

3. Narrow the results. Use the filters on the left to limit by publication year, content type (conferences, journals, standards) and topic.

4. Read the abstract first. It tells you whether a paper is worth your time before you look for the full text.

5. Follow the references. A good paper's reference list and its "cited by" list lead you to related work.

Full-text access depends on your institution's subscription or your IEEE membership options. Check with the library or the branch if you are unsure. More research links are on the Resources page: /resources
